A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Quest research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Full-document comparison supports reliable judgments; the appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: v6 reports original training and benchmark results for Quest, including LongBench, Longbook QA, retrieval evaluations, scaling experiments, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and the HELMET, keyword-quality, and document-similarity experiments in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same query prediction, keyword extraction, inverted indexing, index splitting, oversampling, and document-concatenation procedure. No model or training-objective changes appear.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Pile training data and retain LongBench, Longbook QA, seven short-text benchmarks, HELMET, and the sentence-retrieval and numeric-string Needle-in-a-Haystack scenarios.

E2.justification: Standard, KNN, and ICLM remain the principal comparators. The model comparisons in Table 4, existing-long-document comparison in Table 5, and appendix keyword and KNN strategy comparisons have unchanged membership.

E3.justification: Model sizes, context lengths, training budgets, metrics, sample sizes, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Sections 4–6 and the appendices describe the same experimental settings.

E4.justification: The training-progress, document-similarity, existing-long-document, split-ratio, query-quality, keyword-extraction, keyword-selection, and KNN-strategy analyses are retained unchanged. No ablation or robustness evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: There are no changes to repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty reporting, or statistical estimation. Appendix C.3 retains the same human/GPT-4o evaluation and Pearson-correlation analysis.

E6.justification: Tables 1–17 and Figures 1–11 retain the same numerical results, comparison entries, and empirical trends. Section 4.3 qualifies the interpretation of these outcomes without reporting different measured outcomes.

T1.justification: The oversampling equations in Section 3 and exponential validation-loss scaling formulation in Section 6 are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about query-centric synthesis, balancing relevance and diversity, long-context performance, and scaling predictability. The local qualifications in Section 4.3 do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 changes consistent superiority across tasks to superiority on average. It also qualifies short-text preservation as almost no degradation on average and removes the contrasting statement about other methods degrading. These are more limited interpretations of unchanged results.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, processing and training times, and access links are unchanged, including Appendix A and Table 6. The Needle-in-a-Haystack link moves between pages without changing its content.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to earlier research are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgement introduces no research citation or novelty claim.

P1.justification: v7 makes localized wording revisions in Section 4.3, adds Section 8 acknowledging National Natural Science Foundation of China support, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The broader narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 receives a revised caption. Text, footnotes, and spacing reflow across pages 7–10, including the starts of Sections 5.2 and 5.3. Figures and table structures remain unchanged, with no new or removed displays.

improvement.justification: v7 better aligns its results discussion with the evidence by replacing broad superiority and preservation statements with average-qualified wording. Table 1 contains task-level losses despite higher averages, while Table 3 shows Quest averaging 0.4831 versus Pythia's 0.4830 despite declines on several tasks. This improves interpretive precision; the methods, empirical evidence, and appendices remain unchanged.
